label: The prepare nudge text enumerates the note shape and required sections and never mentions the History Lookup, so a sender cannot know the receiver has a recovery path.
The prepare command's only stdout is the arming line plus the note path; it names no recovery path either.
The Pi sender's note asserted that a fresh session cannot recover the side word and told the receiver to ask the operator, which is true of the note and false of the hop.
The OpenCode sender's note pointed at the claim's History Lookup section for the withheld side word, and that run scored 5/5.
The claim seed text tells the receiver to run claim and read the note body and never names the History Lookup, so the offer appears only in claim stdout after the note body.
The claim output appends the lookup section with a weaker directive than the note's own ask-the-operator line, and prints it after the note body, so the note's claim wins the reading order.
The Pi receiver named the lookup and dismissed it on the note's authority, then asked the operator and left the note claimed.

direction: The Pi lookup was never offered
reason: handoverLookupSection mints the locator at claim time from the note's own session_id, runtime and cwd, all present in the Pi note; the pane capture collapses tool output so its silence is not evidence of absence.

direction: The Pi sender leaked the side word
reason: Both scorecards record sideWordInNote false, so the withholding instruction held on both runtimes.
